tweets.title: Ten thousand years of knowledge on securing wealth is about physical matter, walls, vaults, guards, weight. None of it transfers to bitcoin. Securing bitcoin is a new discipline of civilization, and the first generation of users are writing the manual from a blank page.

Nobody in human history held absolute property before the year 2009 with the invention of a bitcoin hardware wallet, so nobody in history had to learn what we are learning today. Every person who masters self-custody is not following a tradition. They are founding one.
Diversify your keys, not your coins.
tweets.summary: Diversify your keys, not your coins. Jameson Lopp (@lopp) There is no perfect hardware device for securing private keys. They all have different trade-offs, different pros and cons. The way to address weaknesses of hardware devices is by leveraging the magic of additive security.

tweets.title: The reason bitcoin doesn’t change is not that change is forbidden. It’s that the change requires convincing millions of strangers to change Bitcoin who bought it because it doesn’t change.

The Bitcoin developers write the rules but can’t impose them on anyone. The Bitcoin miners follow the rules but can’t change them. The Bitcoin nodes enforce the rules, but only on themselves. The Bitcoin holders own all the money, but the money makes none of the rules.
On this day in history, 16 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto wrote, “If you don’t believe me or don’t get it, I don’t have time to convince you, sorry.”
